S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient_info.stressor: When Lori and her husband began a long-delayed kitchen and back-porch remodeling project, contractors uncovered an active wasp nest in the eaves near the door she used to reach her garden. At first she simply took a different route outside, but over the next 2 years and 5 months, wasps and similar buzzing insects came to provoke immediate fear that felt far beyond the actual risk, and she increasingly avoided gardening, outdoor food-pantry unloading, shoreline walks, and neighborhood garden workshops. She could still manage most home routines, but the avoidance disrupted the community roles and seasonal rhythms that had anchored her life. Lori finally raised the issue with her primary care clinician after she declined to host a church garden day for the second summer in a row and was referred for psychiatric evaluation.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’m here because I’ve gotten to where I plan my whole summer around avoiding wasps, even giving up my garden jobs at church and making my husband unload things by the back porch if I hear buzzing.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I know a wasp is just a little insect and most folks would swat it away, but to me it feels like something terrible is about to happen if one gets anywhere near me.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: The second I hear that sharp buzzing by the porch or see one hovering near the flowers, my heart jumps, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get inside right away.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve had to step back from the church gardening group and stopped hosting garden days, which used to be a big part of how I stayed connected with people. At home, my husband has taken over porch and garden tasks I used to handle myself.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since the remodel uncovered that wasp nest, about two years and five months ago.
